prompt: Write a story about a retired train conductor who finds an unclaimed suitcase. End with a difficult choice rather than a twist. Aim for 500 words.
Write a mystery set in a small bakery. A missing recipe is the central puzzle, and the solution should follow from clues in the story. Aim for 500 words.
Write a science-fiction scene about a gardener on a space station where sunlight is rationed. Aim for 300 words.
Write a fantasy story about a bridge that asks travelers for a memory instead of money. Aim for 300 words.
Write a story for children aged six to eight about a turtle who wants to learn to dance. Aim for 200 words.
Write a funny account of someone trying to assemble a bookshelf with the wrong instructions. Aim for 200 words.
Write a scene entirely in dialogue between two siblings deciding what to do with their father's old chair. Aim for 150 words.
Write a prose poem about a city market after everyone has gone home. Avoid rhyme. Aim for 150 words.
Write an adventure scene about three hikers escaping a gorge as the river rises. Give each hiker a useful role. Aim for 300 words.
Write a fictional scene set at a railway station in 1910, from the perspective of a woman arriving alone in a new town. Aim for 200 words.
Write an essay about Gandhi in South Africa, including his arrival, development of satyagraha, and limitations or controversies in his early views. Keep historical claims accurate. Aim for 500 words.
Write an essay explaining how printing changed the circulation of ideas in early modern Europe. Avoid presenting printing as the sole cause of social change. Aim for 500 words.
Write an essay arguing whether keeping a promise is always the right thing to do. Include a serious counterargument. Aim for 300 words.
Explain how the creature in Mary Shelley's Frankenstein complicates the idea of who the real monster is. Do not invent quotations. Aim for 300 words.
Explain to a general reader why an abstract painting can be meaningful without depicting recognizable objects. Aim for 200 words.
Write a short essay on what can be lost and gained when a poem is translated. Aim for 200 words.
Explain the difference between being alone and feeling lonely without treating either experience as universal. Aim for 150 words.
Explain why a merchant's account book can be valuable to historians even when it says little about ordinary workers. Aim for 150 words.
Write a balanced essay on whether museums should display replicas alongside original objects. Aim for 300 words.
Write a reflective essay about why ordinary household objects can become important family possessions. Aim for 200 words.
Explain the greenhouse effect, distinguishing it from ozone depletion and from short-term weather variation. Write for a curious adult. Aim for 500 words.
Explain how a machine-learning model can perform well on training data and poorly on new data. Use a concrete example and discuss overfitting and data leakage. Aim for 500 words.
Explain natural selection using antibiotic resistance as an example. Distinguish selection from organisms changing because they need to. Aim for 300 words.
Explain why the Moon has phases and why they are not usually caused by Earth's shadow. Aim for 300 words.
Explain why a metal spoon feels colder than a wooden spoon in the same room. Aim for 200 words.
Explain mean and median using the numbers 2, 3, 3, 4, and 13, and show why the distinction matters. Aim for 200 words.
Explain what a computer cache does using an everyday analogy, then mention one way the analogy is imperfect. Aim for 150 words.
Explain why counting planted trees is not the same as measuring a successful urban forest. Aim for 150 words.
Describe a fair experiment to test whether moving recycling signs closer to bins improves sorting. Include a limitation. Aim for 300 words.
Explain the difference between an absence of evidence and evidence of absence with a practical example. Aim for 200 words.
Write a memo for a small repair shop considering evening appointments versus a second location. Recommend a reversible test and explain how to measure it. Aim for 500 words.
Propose a six-week pilot for a shared equipment booking system at a makerspace. Cover scope, responsibilities, success measures, and risks. Aim for 500 words.
Write a fictional incident report about duplicate booking emails caused by a retry bug. No bookings or charges were duplicated. Include timeline, cause, and prevention. Aim for 300 words.
Write a realistic job description for an operations coordinator at a small equipment rental business. Prior experience should be helpful but not required. Aim for 300 words.
Write an apology email to a customer whose replacement desk arrived without mounting brackets. The missing parts will ship tomorrow at no charge. Aim for 200 words.
Write constructive feedback for an analyst whose reports are accurate but who gives late notice of delays. Include a clear next step. Aim for 200 words.
Summarize a fictional meeting where a team agrees to test one onboarding email instead of three, while leaving reminder timing unchanged. Aim for 150 words.
Write a project update: warehouse label pilot begins Monday; six shelf mismatches remain; old codes stay visible during a five-day trial. Aim for 150 words.
Compare buying a cheaper scanner with testing a more expensive one. Discuss total cost and real-world performance without inventing vendor specifications. Aim for 300 words.
Explain a new meeting-room rule: release reservations after ten minutes unless checked in; exempt accessibility arrangements and scheduled maintenance. Aim for 200 words.
Write a clearly fictional feature about a monthly neighborhood repair cafe. Use invented named characters and show both its benefits and limits. Aim for 500 words.
Explain how changing budget categories can make public spending appear to double. Use a clearly hypothetical numerical example and distinguish recurring from one-time costs. Aim for 500 words.
Write a fictional local news article about a public pool reopening after six weeks of repairs. Hours are limited by lifeguard shortages; pass holders receive extensions. Aim for 300 words.
Write a fictional profile of a watch repairer who values explaining uncertainty to customers. Include specific scenes without making the subject flawless. Aim for 300 words.
Write an editorial arguing that transit agencies should explain route changes in plain language and evaluate the changes afterward. Aim for 200 words.
Review an imaginary exhibition of photographs taken in homes just before their occupants move. Include one criticism as well as praise. Aim for 200 words.
Write a fictional match report: Northbank beats Westfield 2–1; Westfield scores first; Northbank's winner comes in the 83rd minute. Aim for 150 words.
Write a news brief about a fictional community center entrance closing Monday through Wednesday. Visitors should use the step-free Willow Lane entrance. Aim for 150 words.
Write a fictional Q&A with a community librarian about the value of libraries beyond borrowing books. Include one challenging question. Aim for 300 words.
Write a nuanced column about the pressure to turn every hobby into an income source. Aim for 200 words.
Write a first-person travel narrative in which a missed express bus leads to a memorable local journey, but the destination is obscured by clouds. Aim for 500 words.
Write a fictional personal statement for a museum studies applicant whose volunteering taught them the value of careful documentation and acknowledging uncertainty. Aim for 500 words.
Write a personal reflection on learning to draw and becoming more comfortable with mistakes. Use a specific incident rather than generic encouragement. Aim for 300 words.
Write a warm family anecdote about a grandfather who labels every jar in his shed, including one containing parts of a long-gone bicycle. Aim for 300 words.
Write a thank-you letter to a friend who helped with a difficult move and left a meal in the refrigerator. Aim for 200 words.
Write a firm but polite complaint about a missed Friday delivery window and an incorrect attempted-delivery status. Ask for a practical resolution. Aim for 200 words.
Invite neighbors to a free Saturday walk, meeting at ten for about one hour. No registration; heavy rain means tea inside the community hall. Aim for 150 words.
Write a sincere condolence message to a friend whose grandmother died. Avoid religious assumptions and claims that you know exactly how they feel. Aim for 150 words.
Write a diary entry about finally clearing a cluttered desk and discovering that the main benefit is a place to rest rather than greater productivity. Aim for 300 words.
Ask an online forum for advice on sharing one small workshop between sewing, model making, and general crafts. There is no space for another large table. Aim for 200 words.
Write a 45-minute lesson plan for twelve-year-olds on distinguishing observation from inference using a closed box. Include timings and an assessment activity. Aim for 500 words.
Write a practical study guide for students preparing for exams that require explanations. Include retrieval practice, spacing, and a realistic weekly example. Aim for 500 words.
Write a balanced argument about letting students choose between an essay, presentation, and model when demonstrating learning. Explain when choice is inappropriate. Aim for 300 words.
Write an interpretive label for a fictional early-twentieth-century worker's wooden lunch box. Distinguish observable evidence from things we cannot know. Aim for 300 words.
Give feedback on a student argument for two extra library hours each weekday. Praise its focus, ask for relevant evidence, and explain why weekend access belongs elsewhere. Aim for 200 words.
Write a parent newsletter about a primary-school project on material properties. Bringing an object is optional; no purchases, glass, sharp tools, or valuables. Aim for 200 words.
Explain how maps use symbols and omit details to an eight-year-old, including why different maps of the same place can be useful. Aim for 150 words.
Write a clear assignment asking students to compare two accounts of the same event and explain disagreements using evidence. Aim for 150 words.
Write a presentation rubric prioritizing claim, evidence, and reasoning over visual polish. Do not penalize nervousness by itself. Aim for 300 words.
Write a teacher's reflection on a group activity that was lively but did not clearly demonstrate learning. Suggest a specific improvement. Aim for 200 words.
Write a launch plan for a fictional compact reading lamp with a physical switch and replaceable bulb. Avoid unsupported performance claims. Aim for 500 words.
Write a believable brand story for a fictional notebook company founded because attractive notebooks would not lie flat. Avoid claiming notebooks transform lives. Aim for 500 words.
Write a clearly fictional case study about a makers club trialing shared booking software for two workstations. Include a limitation and an adoption difficulty. Aim for 300 words.
Write landing-page copy for a fictional service that helps small community groups schedule volunteer shifts. Explain value clearly without promising perfect outcomes. Aim for 300 words.
Describe a fictional folding desk organizer with three compartments and a removable tray. Be clear about its limited storage capacity. Aim for 200 words.
Write a welcome email for a monthly gardening newsletter aimed at people with small spaces. Include what to expect and a simple first activity. Aim for 200 words.
Promote a two-hour beginner bookbinding workshop. Materials are included, places require reservation, and large machines are operated by staff only. Aim for 150 words.
Invite customers to a three-minute survey about Saturday opening hours. Make clear that responses inform but do not guarantee changes. Aim for 150 words.
Compare pocket and large sketchbooks made with identical paper and binding. Explain tradeoffs without claiming one is universally better. Aim for 300 words.
Write an appeal for six replacement tables for a community room. Promise to publish the invoice and explain surplus use; donations do not affect access. Aim for 200 words.
Write a practical guide to packing for a five-day trip with one small bag, including choosing clothes and avoiding unnecessary duplicates. Aim for 500 words.
Explain how a beginner can photograph a household object using window light and a sheet of white card. Include common mistakes and how to check the result. Aim for 500 words.
Explain how to assess sunlight, wind, and drainage before starting a balcony garden. Avoid prescribing one watering schedule for every plant. Aim for 300 words.
Write an entryway organization guide for a shared household, focusing on real habits rather than maintaining a perfect appearance. Aim for 300 words.
Explain how to roast mixed vegetables, accounting for different cooking rates, overcrowding, and how to judge doneness. Aim for 200 words.
Write a clearly fictional review of a travel mug used for two weeks: comfortable grip and useful size, but a lid groove that is hard to clean. Do not invent lab measurements. Aim for 200 words.
Explain how to make a paper accordion with evenly spaced alternating folds. Include one troubleshooting tip. Aim for 150 words.
Explain what to check when a shared printer accepts a job but produces no pages, and why repeatedly resubmitting can cause problems. Aim for 150 words.
Write a balanced guide to deciding whether to repair or replace an ordinary household object. Discuss uncertainty and usefulness, not just purchase price. Aim for 300 words.
Give a beginner advice on starting a small stamp collection, recording uncertainty, and avoiding the assumption that age alone determines value. Aim for 200 words.
Write a policy brief proposing a six-week evening-library-hours trial. Assess new access, costs, and displacement of daytime services rather than just visitor counts. Aim for 500 words.
Evaluate a fictional four-week community shuttle pilot with 480 passenger journeys and high use on market mornings. Costs exceeded estimates; avoided car trips were not measured. Aim for 500 words.
Respond to a proposal to add benches to a town square. Support the aim but request a temporary layout trial and clear maintenance responsibilities. Aim for 300 words.

Write a fictional accessibility review of a step-free hall with obstructive chair storage, unclear signs, and staff unfamiliar with hearing equipment. A single visit is not certification. Aim for 300 words.
Write a short public-meeting speech asking for quieter play options and shaded seating in a new playground, without opposing replacement of worn equipment. Aim for 200 words.
Explain a community garden budget's distinction between operating costs, one-time improvements, expected donations, and reserves. Aim for 200 words.
Welcome reading-room volunteers and explain referring unknown questions to a coordinator, respecting visitors, and making concise handovers. Aim for 150 words.
Explain that a fictional tool library is changing its opening hours for a four-week trial and wants feedback from both users and people unable to attend. Aim for 150 words.
Write a cautious impact summary for a fictional tool library with 140 members and 620 loans. Do not infer money saved or waste avoided directly from loans. Aim for 300 words.
Write a neutral summary of a disagreement between neighbors over a shared garden's quiet hours, identifying common ground and a practical trial agreement. Aim for 200 words.
